answer: Collateral is slashed jointly when correlated behavioural faults fire inside the same window. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The zephyr is the collateral at risk, the cipher the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the haven the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many cipher groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the zephyr into smaller, individually useless stakes.
